task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 1b) hard gate on REQ-165's design at lib/letflow/design/req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md. This design's central claim: wasmex v0.15.1 depends on rustler_precompiled, so a bare `mix deps.get && mix compile` could succeed via a precompiled NIF download WITHOUT invoking cargo/rustc at all -- satisfying the fetch/compile mechanically while violating the requirement's explicit 'a successful fetch alone does not satisfy this' clause. The design's fix is WASMEX_BUILD=true forcing a real source build, and it claims wasmex's own upstream .tool-versions already pins rust 1.97.1. Independently re-verify these claims against the real, current wasmex source/docs -- do not trust the design doc's own account. Also verify the CI mechanism proposed (dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable fed via $GITHUB_OUTPUT, since no version-file: equivalent exists for that action) is technically sound, the handler module design is complete and implementable, and the process-boundary/timeout mechanisms genuinely mirror plugin_interface.ex's real invoke/2,3 code.
acceptance_criteria: Independently verify wasmex v0.15.1's real mix.exs dependencies (via WebFetch to its GitHub repo or hex.pm) include rustler_precompiled and rustler as claimed -- quote the real file.

Independently verify WASMEX_BUILD=true (or an equivalent real, documented mechanism) genuinely forces a source build bypassing precompiled artifacts -- check wasmex's own README/CI docs for this exact env var or the real equivalent.

Independently verify wasmex's own upstream .tool-versions file (via gh api or WebFetch to the raw GitHub content) genuinely pins the rust version the design cites -- quote the real file content and note the exact version.

Confirm the CI mechanism (dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable fed a version via $GITHUB_OUTPUT since no version-file: input exists for that action) is technically sound -- read the real dtolnay/rust-toolchain action's documented inputs to confirm no version-file equivalent actually exists (or if one now does, flag it as a possible simplification).

Confirm the handler module design (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex, @behaviour Letflow.Engine.PluginInterface, handle_node/1) is complete enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without improvising -- check the two .wat fixtures described (trivial answer-returning guest, hanging guest) are correctly specified.

Confirm the process-boundary proof mechanism (self() captured inside handle_node/1, returned in the outcome map) and the timeout mechanism (relying on PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's existing, unedited Task.yield/Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) path) genuinely match plugin_interface.ex's real code -- read invoke/2,3 directly yourself.
Confirm lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex is correctly identified as needing zero edits.

Confirm the moduledoc content specifications (WASM-01 mechanism-clause restatement, residual native-crash-risk disclosure) are worded precisely enough to satisfy the requirement's exact acceptance-criteria wording, and consistent with plugin_interface.ex's own existing disclosed-and-uncovered crash-class language.

All 9 real acceptance criteria mapped in a traceability table; zero literal Elixir function-body code in the design doc (infra config lines and WAT fixtures are not covered by this rule, per the requirement's own nature).
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: Independently re-verified all central claims of lib/letflow/design/req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md against live external sources and the real plugin_interface.ex; every claim checked out exactly as the design states. Design is complete and unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without improvising.

independent_verification.claim: wasmex v0.15.1 mix.exs deps() lists rustler_precompiled ~> 0.9, rustler ~> 0.38, ex_doc, credo
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED verbatim: deps() = [{:rustler_precompiled, "~> 0.9"}, {:rustler, "~> 0.38"}, {:ex_doc, "~> 0.40.3", only: [:dev, :test]}, {:credo, "~> 1.7.19", only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false}]

independent_verification.claim: WASMEX_BUILD=true is wasmex's own documented switch to force a real source build over a precompiled NIF fetch
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED. README line 106: 'If you plan to change something on the Rust part of this project, set the following ENV WASMEX_BUILD=true so that your changes will be picked up.' wasmex's own CI (elixir-ci.yml) sets WASMEX_BUILD: true at workflow env scope and installs dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable unconditionally in every native-code job -- exactly as the design's §0 states, maintainers never trust the precompiled path for their own CI.

independent_verification.claim: wasmex's own upstream .tool-versions pins rust 1.97.1 in the same file-shape as Letflow's own convention
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED verbatim: 'erlang 29.0.3\nelixir 1.20.2-otp-29\nrust 1.97.1'. wasmex's own CI installs it via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with toolchain: 1.97.1, matching the design's citation exactly.

independent_verification.claim: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable has no version-file: equivalent input, justifying the $GITHUB_OUTPUT shell-step workaround
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED -- real documented inputs are toolchain (required), targets, target (alias), components. No version-file/version-from-file input exists; the design's workaround (grep .tool-versions in a preceding shell step, thread the value via $GITHUB_OUTPUT into toolchain:) is the correct, currently-necessary mechanism. Minor inaccuracy found: the design's parenthetical at design doc line 189-190 lists the real inputs as 'toolchain, components, target, profile' -- there is no 'profile' input (that string only appears hardcoded inside the action's internal `rustup toolchain install --profile minimal` step, not exposed as a caller input), and 'targets' (plural) is missing from the design's list. This is a citation slip in an explanatory aside, not load-bearing: it does not affect the actual CI YAML diff in §2 (which only sets `toolchain:`), so it does not change implementability. Flagged as a finding for CODE-DESIGNER to correct in a fast-follow, not a gate failure.

independent_verification.claim: PluginInterface.invoke/2,3's process-boundary and timeout mechanism (Task.Supervisor.async_nolink, Task.yield, Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill), handle_yield_result/4 nil-clause message) matches the design's §4/§5 description exactly
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED. Lines 186-193 show async_nolink under Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor wrapping `handler.handle_node(context)`, piped through Task.yield(timeout_ms) then handle_yield_result/4. The nil clause (lines 221-224) does exactly `Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill)` then returns `{:error, "plugin handler #{inspect(handler)} did not respond within #{timeout_ms}ms"}` -- matching the design's quoted string and mechanism precisely. Letflow.Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor is confirmed already started in lib/letflow/application.ex:45, unchanged by this requirement, matching §4's grep claim.

independent_verification.method: Read the file in full; confirmed no new @callback, no ExecutionContext field, no handle_yield_result/4 clause is needed for this design's scope
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED. The design's §6 file list correctly excludes lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex; nothing in §3-§5 requires touching it.

independent_verification.claim: moduledoc content specs (§7.1/§7.2) are worded consistently with plugin_interface.ex's own existing disclosed-and-uncovered crash-class language
independent_verification.method: Compared design §7.2's required prose against plugin_interface.ex:52-56's actual 'Does NOT cover' paragraph
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED consistent: both name 'a hard kill of the BEAM node itself, or System.halt/0', both state no monitor/task/supervisor observes it from inside the same node. §7.1's WASM-01 mechanism-clause restatement (Rust NIF vs C API, runtime-loaded shared library vs static platform binary) matches REQ-165's requirements.yaml entry verbatim.

independent_verification.method: Diffed docs/requirements.yaml REQ-165's 9 acceptance_criteria against design §8's table and test/specs/REQ-165.md's traceability table
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED 1:1 mapping, no gaps, no extra/renumbered criteria.

independent_verification.claim: handler module design (location, @behaviour, handle_node/1, two .wat fixtures) is complete enough to implement without improvising
independent_verification.method: Read §3 in full; cross-checked mix.exs's existing deps list (confirmed :lua is the current last entry, matching the design's placement instruction) and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex's real @recognised_tools/F1-F8/not_checked/warn_block shape against the design's characterization of it
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED complete: module path, @behaviour, full internal flow (5 numbered steps with exact Wasmex API calls, cleanup-on-every-path instruction), both .wat fixtures given verbatim, and the check_toolchain extension's shape (@recognised_tools, running_rust_version/0 spec, new F9 failure mode) matches the real existing module's structure exactly (verified: @recognised_tools = ["elixir", "erlang"], F1-F8 present, not_checked/warn_block helpers present).

independent_verification.claim: design contains no literal Elixir implementation code (function bodies)
independent_verification.method: Scanned every fenced code block in the design doc
independent_verification.result: CONFIRMED. Only fenced blocks present: one mix.exs dependency-tuple data literal ({:wasmex, "~> 0.15.1"}), shell commands (WASMEX_BUILD=true mix ...), a .tool-versions diff, a ci.yml YAML diff, and two .wat fixtures -- all exempted infra-config/data per AC9's own carve-out. Prose in §3.2/§4/§5 narrates Wasmex API calls (Wasmex.start_link/1, Wasmex.call_function/4, GenServer.stop/1) as running text, never as a def/defp function body. @spec-only declarations throughout, no implementations.
